text:
Marco: hey team, first day question. I set up VPN + SSH to bastion and tried to use local port forwarding to access our private docker registry: `ssh -L 5000:internal.registry.redwood:5000 bastion`. From Windows Docker (WSL2) `docker pull localhost:5000/my-image` returns connection refused. I can `curl http://localhost:5000` from Windows cmd but inside WSL it fails. Any ideas?

Kevin: welcome Marco! this is a WSL/Windows localhost binding quirk. Docker Desktop runs in Windows and WSL uses a separate network namespace. Localhost from WSL != Windows localhost by default.

Marco: ahhh that explains. so why does `curl` work in cmd but not `wsl`?

Priya: exactly. In WSL2 the `localhost` is within the VM. You can reach the Windows host from WSL at `$(cat /etc/resolv.conf | grep nameserver | awk '{print $2}')` or use the special `host.docker.internal` name. Try `curl http://host.docker.internal:5000` from WSL.

Marco: tried `curl http://host.docker.internal:5000` and got a response! docker still can't `docker pull host.docker.internal:5000/my-image` though, Docker says `invalid reference format` if I prefix with `host.docker.internal`?

Sam: Docker requires a hostname (not `localhost`) in the image name and the registry must be HTTP or configured as insecure registry. For testing you can: 1) add "host.docker.internal:5000": {} to Docker Desktop > Settings > Docker Engine insecure-registries, then restart Docker; or 2) in WSL do `export DOCKER_HOST=tcp://host.docker.internal:2375` if you enabled the daemon on tcp (not recommended long-term).

Marco: ok I added `host.docker.internal:5000` to insecure registries and restarted Docker Desktop. `docker pull host.docker.internal:5000/my-image` now starts fetching. Thanks!

Kevin: alternate: when you `ssh -L` you can bind to all interfaces so WSL can reach it via the WSL <-> Windows IP. Example: `ssh -L 0.0.0.0:5000:internal.registry.redwood:5000 -N bastion` then from WSL `curl http://<windows-ip>:5000`. but note `-g` (`Allow remote hosts to connect to local forwarded ports`) is needed for some ssh clients.

Priya: also FYI we have a doc about Docker + WSL quirks in onboarding: https://redwood.internal/onboard/wsl-docker (infra-bot message)

Infra-bot: Automated note: please avoid `--insecure` image pulls in prod. For persistent access to private registries we recommend adding registry to Docker Desktop insecure list or using our auth proxy (see https://redwood.internal/infra/registry-proxy).

Marco: super helpful. two small follow-ups: 1) should I add `host.docker.internal` to NO_PROXY or to Docker settings? 2) is binding `0.0.0.0` safe?

Sam: 1) add `host.docker.internal` to NO_PROXY in WSL and Windows envs to avoid proxying internal registry traffic. 2) `0.0.0.0` is fine for short-term dev but don't expose ports on untrusted networks. If you need a stable workflow we'll set up a dev-proxy route for you.

Marco: thanks all, saving this to my onboarding notes. :raised_hands:
